title: Wind order gave no clear bird richness contrast in four Canada and US samples in 1985-2024
abstract: We tested whether recorded bird richness differed when wind rose or fell during a survey at the same unordered pair of endpoint wind codes. Four models used 36,981 accepted Canada and US BBS runs in 1985-2004 and 2005-2024. Models controlled route-observer and state-year effects, endpoint temperature and sky, date, start time, duration and assistant status. Rising-minus-falling contrasts were -0.067 and -0.085 recorded taxa in Canada, and +0.128 and +0.230 in the US. All four corrected intervals included zero. Checks that omitted duration, used fair weather or kept adjacent wind codes also gave no clear corrected contrast. The test assumes a common additive order contrast across wind pairs. Selected roadside surveys, endpoint reports, few year clusters and unmeasured local changes limit inference. The result does not establish equal detection, a causal weather effect or a climate-change effect. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and a retrieval recipe are included. Record-level external data remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Rising minus falling endpoint wind contrasts in recorded taxa, conditional on exact unordered wind pair and model controls. All four corrected intervals include zero.
